1.title: Dependencies and Lifecycle Rules
1.text: Welcome to Module eight: Dependencies and Lifecycle Rules. It covers the exam area four. Terraform configuration. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do five things. The dependency graph. Implicit and explicit dependencies. The lifecycle block. Forcing replacement. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: four. Terraform configuration. Exam format: a one-hour online-proctored multiple-choice exam on Terraform one point one two. Validated against: the official Terraform Associate version oh oh four exam objectives.

1.title: The dependency graph
1.text: The dependency graph. Terraform builds a dependency graph of all the resources, data sources and modules, then walks the graph.

1.title: The dependency graph, continued
1.text: The dependency graph. The figure shows this: Implicit dependencies come from references; explicit dependencies come from depends on.

1.title: The dependency graph, continued
1.text: The dependency graph. Independent resources. Created in parallel (by default up to ten at a time, set with -parallelism ). Dependent resources. Created after what they depend on. Destroy. In reverse order: dependents first. terraform graph. Prints the graph in D O T format.

1.title: Implicit and explicit dependencies
1.text: Implicit and explicit dependencies. Implicit. How: A reference to another object. Example: subnet id aws subnet dot main dot id. Explicit. How: The depends on meta-argument. Example: depends on aws iam role policy dot app.

1.title: Implicit and explicit dependencies, continued
1.text: Implicit and explicit dependencies. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study.

1.title: Implicit and explicit dependencies, continued
1.text: Implicit and explicit dependencies. Use depends on only when there is a hidden dependency that no reference shows (for example a permission the application needs at start-up). It takes a list of resource or module addresses. Exam tip: References are preferred; depends on is the exception. Over-using depends on makes plans less precise because Terraform then assumes everything may have changed.

1.title: The lifecycle block
1.text: The lifecycle block. The lifecycle meta-argument changes how Terraform creates, updates and destroys one resource. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study.

1.title: The lifecycle block, continued
1.text: The lifecycle block. create before destroy. When a resource must be replaced, create the new one first, then destroy the old one (default is destroy first); avoids downtime and suits resources whose names must be unique. prevent destroy. Any plan that would destroy the resource fails with an error; protects critical data. ignore changes. Ignore changes to the listed arguments, for example tags changed by another tool; all ignores every argument. replace triggered by. Replace this resource when another resource or attribute changes. precondition, postcondition. Custom checks (Module nine).

1.title: The lifecycle block, continued
1.text: The lifecycle block. Default: destroy, then create. - or plus. create before destroy: create, then destroy. plus or -. prevent destroy does not stop terraform destroy from being planned; it makes the plan fail. Removing the resource block from the configuration also removes the protection. Exam tip: create before destroy equals new first, old later. prevent destroy equals error instead of destroy. ignore changes equals accept outside changes to chosen arguments.

1.title: Forcing replacement
1.text: Forcing replacement. terraform apply -replace aws instance dot web replaces that resource in one run. It replaces the old terraform taint command, which is deprecated. Exam tip: Explicit depends on is a last resort. A reference already creates the order; add depends on only for a hidden dependency.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. One resource uses an attribute of another resource. How does Terraform know the order? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: By the implicit dependency from the reference. A reference creates an implicit dependency, and Terraform orders the work from the graph.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. An application needs an I A M policy to exist before it starts, but the resource does not reference the policy. What should be added? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: A depends on meta-argument. depends on declares an explicit dependency when no reference shows it.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. A resource must be replaced without downtime, and the new object should exist before the old one is removed. Which lifecycle rule fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: create before destroy. create before destroy creates the replacement first, then destroys the old object.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. A team wants Terraform to refuse any plan that would delete a production database. Which rule fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: prevent destroy set to true. prevent destroy makes any plan that would destroy the resource fail with an error.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. Another tool changes the tags on instances, and Terraform should stop reporting this as a change. Which rule fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: ignore changes with the tags argument. ignore changes lists arguments whose outside changes Terraform will ignore.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. Which option forces one resource to be replaced in a single apply? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: terraform apply -replace with the resource address. The -replace option replaces the named resource; taint is deprecated.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. How does Terraform order resources? Answer: By a dependency graph built from references and depends on. Question two. When is depends on needed? Answer: For a hidden dependency that no reference shows. Question three. What does create before destroy do? Answer: Creates the new object before destroying the old one.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What does prevent destroy do? Answer: Makes any plan that would destroy the resource fail. Question five. What does ignore changes do? Answer: Ignores outside changes to the listed arguments. Question six. What replaced terraform taint? Answer: apply with the -replace option.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Graph: implicit (references) and explicit (depends on); parallel when independent; destroy in reverse. lifecycle: create before destroy, prevent destroy, ignore changes, replace triggered by, conditions. Replace: - or plus default (destroy first), plus or - with create before destroy; apply -replace.
